title: cache-hf action: path, key and restore-keys are duplicated in the restore and save steps
answers: change the hf datasets cache key in cache-hf
restore-only cache reads a different key than the saver writes
update cache path for hugging face cache action
why does cache-hf have two cache steps
body:
The composite action .github/actions/cache-hf/action.yml defines `path`, `key` and `restore-keys` twice: once in the `actions/cache/restore` step gated by `if: inputs.restore-only == 'true'`, and once in the `actions/cache` step gated by `if: inputs.restore-only != 'true'`.
Any change to the path glob, the key prefix, the hashFiles source (tests/data/test_huggingface_dataset_and_source.py) or the restore-keys must be applied to both steps. Otherwise restore-only consumers look for a different key than the save-enabled job writes, and they silently miss the cache.
The pinned action revision (55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0) also appears in both steps and must be bumped together.
Constraints: The two `if:` conditions must stay mutually exclusive so that exactly one cache step runs per job.
says: Continuous integration jobs are redownloading cached datasets instead of restoring them.
Pull request test runs take too long because dataset caching is silently missed.
Update the dataset cache storage path and key settings across all pipeline steps.
Read-only test pipelines fail to find the dataset cache saved by previous builds.

Any update to the path glob, key prefix, hashFiles source (tests/data/test_huggingface_dataset_and_source.py), restore-keys, or pinned action revision must be applied to both steps. Failing to synchronize both steps causes restore-only consumers to search for mismatched keys and silently miss the cache. The two steps must maintain mutually exclusive if conditions based on inputs.restore-only so exactly one runs per job.
